_doc: Revert-verify mutants for the arbitrary-length-path dedup of req 8a0ed10b review M2: a +, * or ? path yields each node once (SPARQL 1.1 ALP is a set). Pre-existing defect (a node reached from two predecessors was two term objects in a reference-keyed Set), multiplied by sub-property widening. `tree`/`subject` are placeholders (§A145).
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/core/src/infrastructure/sparql/executors/PropertyPathExecutor.ts

P1_one_or_more_result_not_keyed._note: A node reached from two predecessors is yielded twice by + (and by *, which is + plus the start). Also SP30: the free-subject path over the diamond reaches c from a and from b within ONE start, so it needs the same per-start dedup (P4 removes the other half — the duplicate STARTS).

P2_zero_or_more_start_twice._note: A * path whose cycle leads back to the start yields the start twice (once via the cycle, once as the zero-length step).

P3_zero_or_one_start_twice._note: A ? path over a self-loop yields the start twice (zero-length step and the one step). Keyed in O(1) since review round 2 (a linear nodeInSet per node was quadratic on a wide hop).

P4_free_subject_starts_not_deduped._note: A free-subject path enumerates its start nodes by reference: a node occurring in N triples starts the path N times and every row comes back N times (review round 2 MEDIUM).
